# onpager_user (Resource)

Manage a local OnPager user, metadata and active state with a creation-only write-only password.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "initial_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}

resource "onpager_user" "example" {
  display_name = "Example user"
  login        = "example-user"
  email        = "example-user@example.invalid"
  active       = true

  initial_password                 = var.initial_password
  initial_password_change_required = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `display_name` (String) Nonempty display name without NUL or surrounding whitespace. Mutable; sent through an unversioned sparse metadata PATCH.
- `login` (String) Immutable local login, without NUL or surrounding whitespace. The backend Unicode case-folds it and enforces uniqueness, including retained inactive users. The configured spelling is preserved; login_normalized reports the stored value. Changing login replaces the user, deactivating the old UUID. For import, configure the stored login spelling.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the user is active; defaults to true. Creation initially creates an active user, then deactivates it if false. Deactivation revokes sessions and PATs and completes current incident responsibilities. Reactivation does not restore them. Inactive UUIDs remain readable; refresh/import never mutate the user.
- `email` (String) Human email. Omission or null means no email and clears a previously configured email; an empty or whitespace-only string also clears it. The backend trims and Unicode case-folds nonempty input; its observed value is email_normalized. Creation accepts identity text; metadata updates require a valid email address. The configured spelling is preserved until external drift. For import, configure the stored normalized spelling.
- `initial_password` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Creation-only password, required when creating a user. Untrimmed UTF-8: at least 15 Unicode code points and at most 1024 bytes. Write-only: never stored in Terraform state or plan. May be omitted after creation and for import. Later changes are ignored; Terraform never reads, resets or reconciles the user's password.
- `initial_password_change_required` (Boolean, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Creation-only write-only password policy. Omission or null uses the API default true, requiring a password change at next sign-in. Explicit false keeps the initial password without that requirement. Not stored in state; later changes are ignored.

### Read-Only

- `email_normalized` (String) Observed normalized human email, or an empty string when no email is stored. Used to detect external drift while preserving configured input spelling.
- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.
- `login_normalized` (String) Observed backend-normalized local login from the direct UUID read. OIDC-only users and protected bootstrap users cannot be managed by this resource.

## Import

Import using the user UUID, including inactive local users. Configure the
observed normalized `login` and `email` spelling when adopting an existing user.
Omit `email`, or use `null`, if no email is stored. Import does not require an
initial password and never changes credentials or active state. A later apply
reconciles metadata and `active`; specify `active = false` to retain inactivity.
OIDC-only users and the protected bootstrap identity cannot be managed by this
resource. A local user linked to OIDC is supported; OIDC links remain unmanaged.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_user.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_user.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
```

## Initial password

`initial_password` is required when creating a new user. It is write-only and
never saved in Terraform state or plan. Use an ephemeral sensitive input
variable to keep it out of variable artifacts too. Password bytes are sent
unchanged; the API requires at least 15 Unicode code points and at most 1024
UTF-8 bytes. Do not put real passwords in committed HCL or variable files.

`initial_password_change_required` is also creation-only and write-only. Its
omission uses the API default `true`; explicit `false` does not require a change
at next sign-in. Either creation-only argument may be removed after creation.
Changing either value has no effect on an existing user. Terraform never invokes
password reset, reads password values or reconciles later password/policy drift.
Supplying a new login or explicitly replacing a user requires an initial
password again. Do not replace a user to change its password.

## Lifecycle

The resource owns one local user UUID. Login is immutable; changing it replaces
the user. Name/email metadata updates are sparse and unversioned, with no
`If-Match` or revision attribute. Other identity attributes, preferences, roles,
group/team memberships and personal contacts are managed separately.

The backend owns login/email normalization. Configured spelling is preserved
while it matches the observed server value; external email changes are refreshed
and a later apply reconciles the configured email. Omission/null clears email;
an explicit empty or whitespace-only string also clears it. Creating a user
permits identity text without email-format validation; subsequent nonempty email
updates require an email address. Display names and configured logins must be
nonempty, without surrounding whitespace or NUL.

Users are created active. `active = false` creates the identity and then invokes
deactivation; it is not an atomic inactive create. A failed later operation
retains the created UUID and committed partial changes in state.

Control applies eligible sections of the enabled tenant notification template
in the user creation transaction. When managing the template and users in one
apply, add a dependency on the template to the user resource. The
[user notification defaults example](user_notification_defaults.md#example-usage)
shows the resource order. Individual grants can make additional sections
available before the user's first sign-in.

Destroy deactivates the user, revokes sessions/PATs and completes current incident
responsibilities. The UUID, history, role assignments, memberships and reserved
login/email remain. Already inactive users remain inactive. Reactivation does
not restore revoked credentials or completed responsibilities. Use independent
automation credentials when retiring a user. Errors retain state; no physical
deletion, automatic adoption, password reset or dependency unlinking is used.

Retained identities reserve normalized login/email values. Recreating a destroyed
user with the same identity can return `409`; import its UUID and reactivate it
explicitly instead. A case-only login change can conflict for the same reason.

## Permissions

PATs and native service accounts require explicit tenant grants: `users.create`
for creation, `users.read` for refresh/import and destroy's direct read,
`users.update` for metadata, `users.deactivate` for disabling/destroy and
`users.reactivate` for enabling. The Configuration Provisioner builtin role does
not grant user administration. No password-reset permission is required, and no
roles, tokens or memberships are granted implicitly.
